newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa says Zaire envoy is Mobutu representative.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa says Zaire envoy is Mobutu representative.

text.p: South Africa said on Friday that a Zairean envoy who met President Nelson Mandela for talks on bringing peace to his country was fully authorised to talk on behalf of President Mobutu Sese Seko.
A spokesman for Mobutu said on Thursday the envoy, Ngbanda Nzambo Ko Ayumba, had no authority to speak for the Zairean leader who is recuperating in France from cancer treatment.

But a senior official in South African deputy president Thabo Mbeki's office said Mobutu himself had endorsed Ngbanda, his nephew and security adviser, as his representative for talks in South Africa on how to end a five-month conflict with rebels.

"I sat in a meeting in Nice with the deputy president discussing with Mr Mobutu, and when the deputy president asked who will we talk with when we are back at home, (Mobutu) said: 'My envoy who is Mr Ngbanda,'" Frank Chikane, director-general in Mbeki's office, told state radio.
He also told a news conference in Pretoria that Mobutu said Ngbanda, who met Mandela for an hour of talks on Thursday, would represent him in all discussions.
State radio said that while Ngbanda was in South Africa, exchanges between Mobutu and Mandela had taken place which further endorsed Ngbanda.
It said peace talks would resume on Saturday, but gave no details of who would attend or where they would take place. Mandela will be away on an Asian visit.

Mobutu's spokesman had said Ngbanda was in South Africa for personal reasons, not to negotiate. Mobutu has repeatedly said he will not agree to negotiations until all foreign soldiers have withdrawn from Zairean soil.
Mandela met Ngbanda and Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila separately this week to try to persuade the two sides to sit down for face-to-face talks aimed at agreeing a ceasefire.
